text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • First prenatal visit: blood count, ferritin, quantitative hCG, blood group and antibody screen, rubella immunity, hepatitis B surface antigen, HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis C tests; urine culture; influenza vaccine; prenatal vitamin with folic acid
  • Maternal-fetal medicine consultation with a first-trimester ultrasound at 11 weeks for a uterus large for dates: dating, the number of fetuses and, if more than one, chorionicity; nuchal translucency; and fibroids or a molar pregnancy
  • Nausea and vomiting: small, frequent, bland meals, ginger, and doxylamine with pyridoxine at bedtime; return for vomiting that stops her keeping fluids down, weight loss, or dizziness
  • Iron deficiency anemia: ferrous sulfate 325 mg every other day; blood count and ferritin at the anatomy-scan visit, with intravenous iron in the second trimester if there is no response
  • Mood: EPDS in each trimester and after the birth
  • Twin pregnancy care (dichorionic diamniotic): aneuploidy screening by nuchal translucency for each fetus and cell-free DNA, with chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis available; detailed anatomy scans at 18 to 22 weeks; growth scans every four weeks from 20 weeks with discordance calculated; prenatal visits every two to four weeks; weight gain of about 17 to 25 kg; weekly fetal testing may be considered from 36 weeks
  • Preeclampsia prevention: aspirin 81 mg at bedtime from 12 weeks until delivery, because a twin pregnancy is a high-risk factor; blood pressure and urine protein at every visit
  • Preterm birth: teaching on the signs of preterm labor; cervical length at the anatomy scan; no cerclage, pessary, progesterone, or bed rest for a twin pregnancy alone; antenatal corticosteroids if birth before 34 weeks is threatened
  • Gestational diabetes: one-hour glucose challenge at 24 to 28 weeks
  • Delivery plan: birth at 38 0/7 to 38 6/7 weeks in a hospital with a neonatal intensive care unit; vaginal birth while twin A is head down, with an epidural and the operating room ready for twin B; active management of the third stage for the higher risk of hemorrhage; group B streptococcus swab at 36 to 37 weeks; RSV vaccine at 32 to 36 weeks once the season begins in September; Tdap at 27 to 36 weeks

resource.title: Cleopatra synthetic care plan
resource.description: Evaluation of a uterus large for dates in early pregnancy (dating by the last period checked against the crown-rump length under ACOG Committee Opinion 700; multiple pregnancy, dating error, fibroids, and molar pregnancy) and high-risk prenatal care of a dichorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy in a 29-year-old woman under ACOG Practice Bulletin 231 and Committee Opinion 831: chorionicity from the first-trimester scan, aneuploidy screening options in twins (nuchal translucency for each fetus, cell-free DNA, and diagnostic testing), nausea and vomiting of pregnancy, iron deficiency anemia and iron, low-dose aspirin because a twin pregnancy is a high-risk factor for preeclampsia (USPSTF 2021), detailed anatomy scans, growth scans every four weeks with discordance, preterm birth risk and cervical length without cerclage, progesterone, or bed rest for twins alone (ACOG Practice Bulletin 234), gestational diabetes screening, Tdap and seasonal vaccines, a viral gastroenteritis with tightenings at 22 weeks, perinatal mood screening with the EPDS (ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline 4), and a delivery plan for 38 0/7 to 38 6/7 weeks. The episode ends at 33 weeks, before delivery.
